sourcedFrom: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year in these books)
cleanIntro: The PX4 is a rotating-barrel pistol and it strips like nothing else in the Beretta line: the central block/slide adaptor comes off the barrel as its own part, and the barrel itself is removed by TURNING it rather than lifting it out. Work over a table — Beretta says so — and keep the small parts together.

steps.title: Unloaded first, and work over a table
steps.action: Prove the chamber empty before anything else. Beretta's own caution for this job is about parts on the floor: the recoil spring, its guide and the central block/slide adaptor all come loose in the same movement.
steps.aside: It is advisable to perform field stripping and assembly operations over a table to catch components should they drop.
steps.quote: WARNING: Make sure the pistol is unloaded. If not, unload it following the unloading instructions in this manual.
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.25

steps.title: Magazine out, then both sides of the latch DOWN together
steps.action: Press the magazine release and drop the magazine. Then take the disassembly latch with the thumb and index finger of your supporting hand and press BOTH sides downward at the same time. One side alone will not release it — that is the single thing that stops people on a PX4.
steps.aside: Press the magazine release button to remove the magazine
steps.quote: With the thumb and index finger of the supporting hand, simultaneously press the two sides of the disassembly latch downwards
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.25

steps.title: Nudge the slide forward, then run it off
steps.action: With the latch held down, push the slide gently forward while pressing on its rear, then pull the whole slide-barrel assembly off the frame — central block/slide adaptor, recoil spring and spring guide still in it.
steps.quote: Gently push the slide towards the thumb of the hand which is holding the pistol while pressing on the rear part of the slide
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.25

steps.title: Sights DOWN, and the central block/slide adaptor comes out
steps.action: Turn the slide so the sights face DOWNWARD, then take the central block/slide adaptor, recoil spring and spring guide off the barrel together. The orientation is not incidental: the parts are held in place by gravity at this point in the strip.
steps.aside: Pull out the recoil spring from the central block/slide adaptor
steps.quote: remove the central block/slide adaptor, recoil spring and recoil spring guide from the barrel
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.25

steps.title: ⛔ Now TURN the barrel out — do not lift it
steps.action: Hold the slide with the sights UP and the front sight slightly higher, then rotate the barrel counter-clockwise as seen from the rear and it comes free. A tilting-barrel habit does not work here; the PX4's barrel unlocks by rotation and it leaves the slide the same way. That is the strip complete.
steps.quote: Holding the slide with the sights turned upward and slightly inclined (front sight higher), remove the barrel by rotating the barrel itself (counter-clockwise looking at it from the rear)
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.25

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end — the caution here is specific
steps.action: Brush in from the chamber and scrub chamber and bore, solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one emerges clean. Beretta's warning is narrower than the usual one and worth reading exactly: do not push the brush in from the MUZZLE while the barrel is still in the pistol.
steps.aside: Cleaning the barrel from the breech (chamber) end will avoid damaging the muzzle or bore.
steps.quote: Insert the brush into the barrel from the chamber and scrub the chamber and bore thoroughly. If necessary, first clean the bore with a gun solvent.
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.39

steps.title: The double cam and locking lugs are the working surfaces
steps.action: On a rotating-barrel pistol the double cam and the locking lugs do all the unlocking work, so they are the surfaces that must be clean and then lightly oiled. Cotton cloth with gun oil, brush only if it needs it.
steps.aside: Lightly oil the barrel double cam, the locking lugs and the bore. Lightly oil the outside of the barrel.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel double cam and locking lugs with a cotton cloth soaked in gun oil; If necessary use the supplied brush.
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.39

steps.title: Central block/slide adaptor: the tooth and the spring-guide hole
steps.action: Clean the central block/slide adaptor with an oiled cloth, paying attention to the block tooth and the spring guide hole — the two features that carry the rotation. Dry it carefully, then oil lightly.
steps.quote: Clean the central block/slide adaptor with a cloth soaked in gun oil paying particular attention to the block tooth and the spring guide hole.
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.39

steps.title: Breech face, extractor, rails, locking recesses
steps.action: Oiled cloth over the slide with attention to the breech face, the extractor, the slide rails, the locking shoulders and the locking recesses — then dry the surfaces and oil the slide lightly.
steps.aside: Lightly oil the recoil spring and the spring guide assembly with gun oil. After extensive use it may be necessary to first clean these parts using the supplied brush and gun oil.
steps.quote: Clean the slide with a cloth
steps.cite: Beretta PX4 COMPACT User Manual — C62353/003 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.39

deepAbsentReason: Beretta stops the owner at the field strip on the PX4 and prints it on the page — "No further disassembly is recommended unless done by a competent gunsmith." ⛔ AND THE ONE DEEPER PROCEDURE THE BOOK DESCRIBES IS GUNSMITH ONLY BY NAME: the hammer unit mechanism is built to be extracted from the frame without special tools, and Beretta still says "This operation must be carried out by a competent gunsmith." That it is easy is not that it is permitted. It is carried as a prohibition rather than a deep-clean branch, and nothing is borrowed from a weaker source to fill the gap.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brush in from the CHAMBER end and all the way through before pulling back
Solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one comes out clean
⛔ Never clean the barrel with the pistol assembled
Light oil on the whole barrel before it goes back

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BREECH FACE
tasks: Cloth or nylon brush on the breech face, extractor, rails and locking shoulders
Dry the slide surfaces, then lightly oil the guides

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY
tasks: Light gun oil on the spring guide assembly
Nylon brush first if it is heavily fouled — never a steel one

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Fouling off the frame rails and the magazine well
Magazine lips and follower cleaned, then wiped with a lightly oiled rag
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Recoil spring and spring guide assembly into the block, pointed end first.
Slide held sights-DOWN, barrel entered into its seat slightly inclined with the double cam facing upward.
Push the barrel against the slide head and rotate it axially so the locking lugs lodge in the recesses of the slide.
Block, spring and guide mounted with the flat head of the guide in the hole of the slide below the barrel muzzle, then pushed forward so the block tooth engages the barrel double cam.
Slide turned over and the frame guides re-entered in the slide rails.
⛔ Watch the block centre itself in its frame seat, then retract the slide a few millimetres past the rear of the frame until it CLICKS into the locked position.
Retract the slide to check assembly, then decock the hammer.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: retract the slide a few millimetres beyond the rear of the frame until it clicks into the locked position, then cycle it fully several times and confirm it returns to battery. Decock with the safety/decocking lever if the pistol has one. If the slide will not click home, the block is not centred in its frame seat — take it apart and start that step again rather than forcing it.
